title: Why a big learning rate blows up
audience: Readers who know a model is trained by gradient descent but have not seen why the learning rate has an upper limit.
idea: Each step multiplies the loss by (1 - 2 × rate) squared, so it falls for rates under 1 and grows past it.

weight.label: Weight
weight.formula: (1 - 2 × rate) to the power of steps

beats.title: One step of gradient descent
beats.goal: See that a step moves the weight against its slope by a fixed fraction of that slope.
beats.misconception: That a bigger step always gets to the minimum sooner.

figure.question: How does one step turn a weight into the next weight?

beats.title: The rate sets how fast the loss falls
beats.goal: Connect a larger rate with a smaller loss factor, up to the rate that lands on the minimum.

figure.question: How fast does the loss fall at this rate?

ask.prompt: After ten steps, which learning rate leaves the smaller loss?

beats.title: Past a rate of one, the loss grows
beats.goal: Find the rate where each step stops shrinking the loss and starts growing it.

figure.question: Does the loss fall, stay flat or climb at this rate?

ask.prompt: Find the largest learning rate on the slider that still makes the loss fall.
